\section*{Abstract}
\logpage{[ 0, 0, 1 ]}
 The \textsf{SmallClassNr} package provides access to finite groups with small class number. Currently,
it contains the finite groups of class number at most 14. \mbox{}}\\[1cm]

\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{The SmallClassNr package}}\label{Chapter_package}
\logpage{[ 1, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7EC4E71A8078695B}{}
{
  

 This is the manual for the \textsf{GAP} 4 package \textsf{SmallClassNr} version 1.5.1, developed by Sam Tertooy. 

 
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Installation}}\label{Chapter_package_Section_installation}
\logpage{[ 1, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8360C04082558A12}{}
{
  If you are using \textsf{GAP} version 4.15.0 or newer, then \textsf{SmallClassNr} should be installed by default. 

 If this is not the case, but the \textsf{PackageManager} package is installed and loaded, you can install \textsf{SmallClassNr} from within a \textsf{GAP} session using \texttt{InstallPackage} (\textbf{PackageManager: InstallPackage}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@InstallPackage( "SmallClassNr" );|
  ...
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 

 Alternatively, you can download \textsf{SmallClassNr} as a .tar.gz archive \href{https://github.com/stertooy/SmallClassNr/releases/download/v1.5.1/SmallClassNr-1.5.1.tar.gz} {here}. After extracting, you should place it in a suitable \texttt{pkg} folder. For example, on a Debian\texttt{\symbol{45}}based Linux distribution
(e.g. Ubuntu, Mint), you can place it in \texttt{\$HOME/.gap/pkg} (recommended) which makes it available for just yourself, or in the \textsf{GAP} installation directory (\texttt{gap\texttt{\symbol{45}}X.Y.Z/pkg}) which makes it available for all users. 

 You can use the following command to efficiently install the package for
yourself: 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@A,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Command]
  wget -qO - https://[...].tar.gz | tar xzf - --one-top-level=$HOME/.gap/pkg
\end{Verbatim}
 

 }

 
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Loading}}\label{Chapter_package_Section_loading}
\logpage{[ 1, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X861ED1338181C66D}{}
{
  Once installed, loading \textsf{SmallClassNr} can be done by using \texttt{LoadPackage} (\textbf{Reference: LoadPackage}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@LoadPackage( "SmallClassNr" );|
  ...
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 

 }

\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Classification}}\label{Chapter_classification}
\logpage{[ 2, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8053C9E57C4C5F94}{}
{
  

 The \emph{class number} $k(G)$ of a group $G$ is the number of conjugacy classes of $G$. In 1903, Landau proved in \cite{land03-a} that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, there are only finitely many finite groups with exactly $n$ conjugacy classes. The \textsf{SmallClassNr} package provides access to the finite groups with class number at most $14$. These groups were classified in the following papers: 
\begin{itemize}
\item  $k(G) \leq 5$, by Miller in \cite{mill11-a} and independently by Burnside in \cite{burn11-a}
\item  $k(G) = 6,7$, by Poland in \cite{pola68-a}
\item  $k(G) = 8$, by Kosvintsev in \cite{kosv74-a}
\item  $k(G) = 9$, by Odincov and Starostin in \cite{os76-a}
\item  $k(G) = 10,11$, by Vera L{\a'o}pez and Vera L{\a'o}pez in \cite{ll85-a}
\item  $k(G) = 12$, by Vera L{\a'o}pez and Vera L{\a'o}pez in \cite{ll86-a}
\item  $k(G) = 13, 14$, by Vera L{\a'o}pez and Sangroniz in \cite{vs07-a}
\end{itemize}
 Remarks: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item  In \cite{ll85-a}, three distinct groups of the form $(C_5 \times C_5) \rtimes C_4$ order $100$ with class number $10$ are given. However, only two such groups exist, being the ones with \texttt{IdClassNr} equal to \texttt{[10,25]} and \texttt{[10,26]}.
\item  In \cite{ll86-a}, 48 groups with class number 12 are listed. There are actually 51 such
groups, the three groups missing in \cite{ll86-a} are provided in the appendix of \cite{vs07-a}. These are the groups with \texttt{IdClassNr} equal to \texttt{[12,13]}, \texttt{[12,16]} and \texttt{[12,39]}.
\end{enumerate}
 }

\hyperdef{L}{X7D2B74F9802686C1}{}
{
  

 
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Selecting groups by their ID's}}\label{Chapter_library_Section_groupsbyids}
\logpage{[ 3, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7F2B2BB683990EC7}{}
{
  

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SmallClassNrGroup}}
\logpage{[ 3, 1, 1 ]}\nobreak
\label{AutoDoc_generated_group1}
\hyperdef{L}{X7F0BD3117CA1B4FE}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SmallClassNrGroup({\mdseries\slshape k, i})\index{SmallClassNrGroup@\texttt{SmallClassNrGroup}}
\label{SmallClassNrGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SmallClassNrGroup({\mdseries\slshape k, i: AsPermGroup})\index{SmallClassNrGroup@\texttt{SmallClassNrGroup}!with AsPermGroup}
\label{SmallClassNrGroup:with AsPermGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th finite group of class number \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}} in the library. 



 By default, if the group is soluble, it is given as a PcGroup whose Pcgs is a
SpecialPcgs. If the group is not soluble, or if the option \texttt{AsPermGroup} is added, it will be given as a permutation group of minimal permutation
degree and with a minimal generating set. 

 }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SmallClassNrGroup( 4, 4 );|
  <pc group of size 12 with 3 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G := SmallClassNrGroup( 4, 4 : AsPermGroup );|
  Group([ (1,2,3), (1,4,2) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NrConjugacyClasses( G );|
  4
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsAlternatingGroup( G );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IdClassNr}}
\logpage{[ 3, 1, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8651368082BCE413}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IdClassNr({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IdClassNr@\texttt{IdClassNr}}
\label{IdClassNr}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
the \textsf{SmallClassNr} ID of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, i.e. a pair \texttt{[\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}}]} such that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is isomorphic to \texttt{SmallClassNrGroup(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}})}. 



 

 }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IdClassNr( AlternatingGroup( 4 ) );|
  [ 4, 4 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Selecting groups by their properties}}\label{Chapter_library_Section_groupsbyprops}
\logpage{[ 3, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X840A70BF809216FD}{}
{
  

 For each of the functions in this section, the arguments \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape arg}} must come in pairs consisting of a function and a value (or list of accepted
values). At least one of the functions must be \texttt{NrConjugacyClasses}. Missing functions will be interpreted as \texttt{NrConjugacyClasses}, missing values as \texttt{true}. 

 

 

 The option \texttt{AsPermGroup} can be added to the functions in this section to ensure that all groups are
returned as PermGroups (instead of PcGroups if they are soluble). 

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AllSmallClassNrGroups}}
\logpage{[ 3, 2, 1 ]}\nobreak
\label{AutoDoc_generated_group2}
\hyperdef{L}{X87052993834D10C5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AllSmallClassNrGroups({\mdseries\slshape arg...})\index{AllSmallClassNrGroups@\texttt{AllSmallClassNrGroups}}
\label{AllSmallClassNrGroups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AllSmallClassNrGroups({\mdseries\slshape arg...: AsPermGroup})\index{AllSmallClassNrGroups@\texttt{AllSmallClassNrGroups}!with AsPermGroup}
\label{AllSmallClassNrGroups:with AsPermGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
all finite groups with certain properties as specified by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape arg}}. 



 

 }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@AllSmallClassNrGroups( IsSolvable, true, NrConjugacyClasses, 6 );|
  [ <pc group of size 6 with 2 generators>,
    <pc group of size 12 with 3 generators>,
    <pc group of size 12 with 3 generators>,
    <pc group of size 18 with 3 generators>,
    <pc group of size 18 with 3 generators>,
    <pc group of size 36 with 4 generators>,
    <pc group of size 72 with 5 generators> ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@AllSmallClassNrGroups( [ 3 .. 5 ], IsNilpotent );|
  [ <pc group of size 3 with 1 generator>,
    <pc group of size 4 with 2 generators>,
    <pc group of size 4 with 2 generators>,
    <pc group of size 5 with 1 generator>,
    <pc group of size 8 with 3 generators>,
    <pc group of size 8 with 3 generators> ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@AllSmallClassNrGroups( [ 3 .. 5 ], IsNilpotent : AsPermGroup );|
  [ Group([ (1,2,3) ]),
    Group([ (1,2,3,4) ]),
    Group([ (1,2), (3,4) ]),
    Group([ (1,2,3,4,5) ]),
    Group([ (1,2), (1,3)(2,4) ]),
    Group([ (1,2,3,4)(5,6,7,8), (1,5,3,7)(2,8,4,6) ]) ]
\end{Verbatim}
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OneSmallClassNrGroup}}
\logpage{[ 3, 2, 2 ]}\nobreak
\label{AutoDoc_generated_group3}
\hyperdef{L}{X7AD22E3083C09796}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OneSmallClassNrGroup({\mdseries\slshape arg...})\index{OneSmallClassNrGroup@\texttt{OneSmallClassNrGroup}}
\label{OneSmallClassNrGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OneSmallClassNrGroup({\mdseries\slshape arg...: AsPermGroup})\index{OneSmallClassNrGroup@\texttt{OneSmallClassNrGroup}!with AsPermGroup}
\label{OneSmallClassNrGroup:with AsPermGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
one finite group with certain properties as specified by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape arg}}. 



 

 }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OneSmallClassNrGroup( 6, IsSolvable, false );|
  Group([ (1,2,3)(4,5,6), (1,4)(2,7) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OneSmallClassNrGroup( 10, IsSolvable, true, IsNilpotent, false );|
  <pc group of size 28 with 3 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OneSmallClassNrGroup( 10, IsSolvable, true, IsNilpotent, false : AsPermGroup );|
  Group([ (1,2,3,4,5,6,7), (2,7)(3,6)(4,5)(8,9,10,11) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{NrSmallClassNrGroups}}
\logpage{[ 3, 2, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X84004D087859AF4F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrSmallClassNrGroups({\mdseries\slshape arg...})\index{NrSmallClassNrGroups@\texttt{NrSmallClassNrGroups}}
\label{NrSmallClassNrGroups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
the number of finite groups with certain properties as specified by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape arg}}. 



 

 }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NrSmallClassNrGroups( 14 );|
  93
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NrSmallClassNrGroups( IsSolvable, true, NrConjugacyClasses, 6 );|
  7
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NrSmallClassNrGroups( [ 3 .. 5 ], IsNilpotentGroup );|
  6
\end{Verbatim}
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IteratorSmallClassNrGroups}}
\logpage{[ 3, 2, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D2BB4B379563D9A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IteratorSmallClassNrGroups({\mdseries\slshape arg...})\index{IteratorSmallClassNrGroups@\texttt{IteratorSmallClassNrGroups}}
\label{IteratorSmallClassNrGroups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
an iterator that iterates over the finite groups with properties as specified
by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape arg}}. 



 

 }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@iter := IteratorSmallClassNrGroups( 12, IsSimpleGroup );|
  <iterator>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@for G in iter do Print( Size( G ), "\n" ); od;|
  3420
  5616
  443520
\end{Verbatim}
 }

\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{The Small Groups Library}}\label{Chapter_otherlibraries_Section_smallgrp}
\logpage{[ 4, 1, 0 ]}

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IdClassNrToIdGroup}}
\logpage{[ 4, 1, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C5BB3197F5351D8}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IdClassNrToIdGroup({\mdseries\slshape k, i})\index{IdClassNrToIdGroup@\texttt{IdClassNrToIdGroup}}
\label{IdClassNrToIdGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a pair of integers \texttt{[x, y]} such that \texttt{SmallGroup(x, y)} is isomorphic to \texttt{SmallClassNrGroup(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}})}. 



 

 }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IdClassNrToIdGroup( 9, 19 );|
  [ 192, 1025 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IdClassNr( SmallGroup( 192, 1025 ) );|
  [ 9, 19 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{The Library of Finite Perfect Groups}}\label{Chapter_otherlibraries_Section_perfgrp}
\logpage{[ 4, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8660CD057B7BBD7F}{}
{
  This library is provided by \textsf{GAP} itself. 

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IdClassNrToPerfGrp}}
\logpage{[ 4, 2, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7CA882467C69C584}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IdClassNrToPerfGrp({\mdseries\slshape k, i})\index{IdClassNrToPerfGrp@\texttt{IdClassNrToPerfGrp}}
\label{IdClassNrToPerfGrp}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a pair of integers \texttt{[x, y]} such that \texttt{PerfectGroup(x, y)} is isomorphic to \texttt{SmallClassNrGroup(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}})}. 



 

 }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IdClassNrToPerfGrp( 10, 36 );|
  [ 14520, 1 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IdClassNr( PerfectGroup( 14520, 1 ) );|
  [ 10, 36 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{The Primitive Permutation Groups Library}}\label{Chapter_otherlibraries_Section_primgrp}
\logpage{[ 4, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7FB77CB979750C5D}{}
{
  This library is provided by the \textsf{PrimGrp} package. 

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IdClassNrToPrimGrp}}
\logpage{[ 4, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8146A37D7F89659B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IdClassNrToPrimGrp({\mdseries\slshape k, i})\index{IdClassNrToPrimGrp@\texttt{IdClassNrToPrimGrp}}
\label{IdClassNrToPrimGrp}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a pair of integers \texttt{[x, y]} such that \texttt{PrimitiveGroup(x, y)} is isomorphic to \texttt{SmallClassNrGroup(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}})}. 



 

 }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IdClassNrToPrimGrp( 9, 25 );|
  [ 49, 25 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IdClassNr( PrimitiveGroup( 49, 25 ) );|
  [ 9, 25 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }
